name: McPhee Structure Derivation Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for a structure derived from a corpus by the coding-and-sorting procedure. Scores the process artifacts, not the prose. Average must be >= 3.5; a score below 3 on Dual Sort Integrity or Juxtaposition Discipline requires rework regardless of the average.

criteria.name: Coding Quality
criteria.description: Whether the corpus was cold-read and then coded into sortable, sourced, dated cards with topic codes rather than document-part labels

scores.1: No cards; the corpus was summarized into sections directly
scores.2: Cards exist but codes are document parts (BACKGROUND, ANALYSIS) or lack dates and sources
scores.3: Topic codes with sources, but dates are patchy and typicality is unlabelled
scores.4: Cold read recorded; topic codes pass the four code-quality tests; every card carries source and date or sits in the dated-unknown pile
scores.5: As 4, plus kind and typicality labelled on every card, and undated material explicitly quarantined rather than guessed into position

criteria.name: Dual Sort Integrity
criteria.description: Whether both a strict chronology sort and a strict theme sort were actually run and written down, with a disagreement log produced

scores.1: Only a thematic grouping exists; concept-named sections hold time-scrambled evidence (theme-sort capture)
scores.2: One sort written down, the other asserted to have been run; no disagreement log
scores.3: Both sorts written down; disagreement log present but partial or vague about the nature of each conflict
scores.4: Both sequences written in full; every materially disagreeing card logged with the nature of the conflict
scores.5: As 4, plus each row states its resolution and required artifact, and near-agreement (if claimed) is explicitly justified by the material

criteria.name: Chronology-First Resolution
criteria.description: Whether disagreements resolved toward chronology by default, with any theme-driven break justified and given a named re-entry point

scores.1: Theme won throughout with no justification; the timeline is unrecoverable
scores.2: Multiple unjustified breaks from chronology; flashbacks with no re-entry points
scores.3: Chronology mostly won, but at least one break lacks a stated justification or a named re-entry card
scores.4: Every break from chronology names its justifying theme and its explicit dated re-entry point
scores.5: As 4, plus theme-driven breaks carry a concrete common denominator written as a noun phrase, and interior chronology is restored inside each panel

criteria.name: Juxtaposition Discipline
criteria.description: Whether each white-space argument passed the state-and-footnote gate, avoided adjacency-as-causation, and stayed within budget

scores.1: Juxtapositions imply causation or motive the evidence does not support, and none is written out
scores.2: Inferences not written out; pairs kept on aesthetic grounds; no budget applied
scores.3: Inferences written out, but at least one would not survive being stated and cited, or the pairs echo rather than revise
scores.4: Every pair has a written inference that passes the footnote test, ordered so the second card revises the first, budget respected
scores.5: As 4, plus rejected candidates recorded with the reason, and system-protagonist personification capped and counted

criteria.name: Shape Naming and Invisibility
criteria.description: Whether the resolved sequence carries a real shape name with a stated emergence test, and whether roadmap sentences were stripped

scores.1: No shape named; the structure is described as 'a mix' or left implicit
scores.2: A shape label asserted with no emergence test, or a hybrid label invented to end the sorting step
scores.3: Shape named with a plausible test, but the invisibility test was not run
scores.4: Shape named with its emergence test stated about the actual cards; invisibility test run and roadmap sentences removed
scores.5: As 4, plus runner-up shape named with the reason it lost, and any surviving signposting justified as navigation furniture for an obligated reader

criteria.name: Evidence Custody
criteria.description: Whether discarded material was logged with did-not-support separated from contradicted, and contradicting cards routed into the body

scores.1: Material that did not fit the shape was dropped silently
scores.2: A single undifferentiated discard list; contradicting evidence not distinguished
scores.3: Two categories present, but contradicting cards are relegated to endnotes or a closing qualifications block
scores.4: Two categories maintained; every contradicting card assigned a position in the body
scores.5: As 4, plus each contradicting card's effect on confidence in the shape is stated, and cards invented to fill holes are demonstrably absent

criteria.name: Refusal Capability
criteria.description: Whether the derivation was willing to report that the corpus supports no shape, rather than manufacturing one

scores.1: A shape was imposed on independent findings, manufacturing causality the corpus does not support
scores.2: Refusal conditions present in the material but unacknowledged; the shape was forced
scores.3: Refusal conditions acknowledged in passing, then worked around without explanation
scores.4: Refusal conditions checked explicitly; either a shape is justified against them or the no-shape finding is reported
scores.5: As 4, plus multi-causal material was braided or split rather than flattened, with the set-aside contradiction named and explained

criteria.name: Contract and Handoff
criteria.description: Whether an immutable shape contract was produced and the component piles were made ready for downstream drafting

scores.1: No contract; drafting began before the shape was fixed, or the lede was written first
scores.2: Shape stated informally; no record of flashbacks, juxtapositions or contradicting cards
scores.3: Contract present but incomplete; components not separated into piles
scores.4: Full contract (shape, runner-up, flashbacks with re-entry points, juxtapositions, contradicting cards); components piled; lede written last
scores.5: As 4, plus the contract is marked immutable with a logged-restart rule, and the handoff to writing-structure-planner is explicit

passing_note: Average score must be >= 3.5. Scores below 3 in 'Dual Sort Integrity' or 'Juxtaposition Discipline' require rework regardless of the average: the first indicates theme-sort capture, the second indicates uncited claims placed in white space.
